The only signal was the open PR. **Guard (this FIX, FIX-461):** (1) `--check` now fails when any currently-completed FIX-ID's only resolvable commit SHAs are off-trunk (detection — would have failed CI on b68c310f's push-to-main); uses 'any completing SHA is an ancestor' semantics so the FIX-435 orphan-plus-landed duplicate is not a false positive, and skips sentinel SHAs (backfill/reopen) + shallow-clone-missing objects. (2) `scanCommits()` filters out completions whose commit is not an ancestor of trunk (origin/main, fallback main) so premature rows can't be written in the first place; falls back to current behavior when no trunk ref resolves. (3) `pnpm fixes:check` wired into `.github/workflows/tests.yml` (fetch-depth:0) as a blocking job. Tests added in test-fixes-sync.mjs for the pure decision core. <!--id:FIX-461-->
- [x] 🟠 L — **Nightly fec-phase times out every Sunday (FEC bulk + IRS 990 exceeds 120-min budget)** — Recurring, confirmed against prod data_sync_log + GHA run logs. The nightly-sync `fec-phase` job (.github/workflows/nightly.yml) is cancelled at ~120m wall-clock **every Sunday** — runs 2026-05-17, 2026-05-24, 2026-05-31 all hit the timeout-minutes:120 ceiling; weekdays finish in 10-45m. Sunday is the heavy day (FEC bulk individual donations + IRS 990). At kill time (run 26705214757, 08:19 UTC) the job was mid indiv-to-committee upsert with many chunks failing `canceling statement due to statement timeout` (Postgres statement_timeout on per-chunk upserts), which drags wall-clock until the job SIGTERM. NOT OOM, NOT an upstream API error, NOT the FIX-430 ai-tagger code (that runs in enrichment-phase, which ran 0s — `needs: fec-phase` skipped it). Because fec-phase is cancelled, **enrichment-phase never runs on Sundays** (LittleSis, EDGAR weekly, USASpending, CourtListener, MV refreshes, AI taggers/summaries all skipped) → prod data progressively staler each week. This is the same failure mode FIX-292 split the job to fix, now recurring within the single fec-phase budget. **Secondary observability bug:** the Sunday kill writes ZERO data_sync_log rows — runNightlySync writes only a terminal (complete/partial) row, never a 'running' start-row, so mark-killed.ts finds no orphan and writes no synthetic nightly_killed row. Every Sunday kill is therefore classified `missing` (not `killed`) by the canary — confirmed: canary_check meta rows show missing_dates 2026-05-17 → 2026-05-24 → 2026-05-31. The canary DID alert (missing_count:1 each Sunday), so it was not silent. **Remediation options (needs decision, see also [[FIX-292]]):** (a) split fec-phase further so FEC-bulk-indiv and IRS-990 each get their own 120-min job; (b) raise/bypass statement_timeout for the bulk indiv/indiv-to-committee chunk upserts (route via direct pg.Client like lib/heavy-rebuild.ts) and/or enlarge chunk size to cut round-trips; (c) decouple Sunday enrichment-phase from fec-phase completion so enrichment still runs when FEC bulk overruns; (d) raise timeout-minutes (blunt). Also fix mark-killed/runNightlySync to write a 'running' start-row so kills register as `killed` not `missing`. Investigation: docs/audits or this session's notes; run logs gh run view 26705214757. <!--id:FIX-462-->

Before FEC bulk even starts, the daily Phase-1 Congress pipeline wastes ~27 min on queries that EVERY time fail with `canceling statement due to statement timeout`: the `promote-candidates` stage (runOfficialsPipeline) failed on ~165 consecutive officials at ~8s each (06:21→06:43, ~22 min), then the House/Senate vote `skip-check` loads (runVotesPipeline) timed out (06:43→06:48, ~5 min). Same root cause as FIX-462's indiv upserts and [[FIX-444]]: prod PostgREST role/statement_timeout (~8s) on queries that have grown slow against now-large tables (officials, votes). Each failure burns the full timeout with zero progress. FIX-462 (direct-pg for the indiv upserts) leaves fec-phase comfortably under its 120-min budget even with this 27-min sink present, so it is non-fatal post-FIX-462 — but it is pure waste and a latent re-timeout risk as data grows. Fix: route the promote-candidates upsert and the votes skip-check existence loads through a direct `pg.Client` with a raised SESSION statement_timeout (precedent: lib/heavy-rebuild.ts `selectDirect`/`runHeavyRebuild`), and/or make the skip-check a single batched existence query instead of per-roll loads. Investigation needed: identify WHY each query is slow (missing index? full scan?) — the timeout may be masking a query that should be sub-second with the right index. Files: packages/data/src/pipelines/congress/* (officials promote-candidates, votes skip-check). <!--id:FIX-463-->
- [x] 🟠 M — **Parallel-session collision guards: pre-push fixes:check, session:check, per-FIX worktree workflow** — Three collision classes all stemmed from >1 writer touching one checkout's `.git` (VSCode git extension + an agent contending): a stranded PR whose FIXes `fixes:sync` recorded as shipped while the code sat unmerged ([[FIX-461]]), stale `index.lock`, and a corrupted `.git/config` line. Enforce a serialize-by-default model: (1) tracked `.githooks/pre-push` runs `pnpm fixes:check` and aborts the push on FIXES.md/done.log drift, wired via `core.hooksPath` from a root `prepare` script (no husky, no new deps); (2) `pnpm session:check` — read-only start-of-session reconciliation (fetch, ahead/behind, worktrees, unmerged branches, open PRs, fixes:check); (3) `pnpm session:worktree <id>` / `:done <id>` — per-FIX worktrees in a sibling dir outside the repo, both `.env.local` seeded to LOCAL Docker, `:done` refuses to remove unmerged work without --force. Primary VSCode checkout stays parked on `main` and agents never commit there; `main` advances only by ff from a rebased branch; `fixes:sync` runs only after merge. CLAUDE.md updated (first-step + Parallel sessions convention). Tooling+docs only, no app deploy. <!--id:FIX-464-->

(FIX-461)`) matched as a trailer and — non-global, first-match-wins, and appearing before the real `Fixes:` line — shadowed it, attributing the commit to the wrong FIX. Surfaced when the [[FIX-464]] commit body mentioned `fixes:sync` in prose: sync then wanted to log FIX-461 instead of FIX-464 and skip flipping FIX-464's checkbox. Fix: make fixesRe/closesRe/verifiedRe/verifiedPerFixRe case-SENSITIVE (git trailer keys are always capitalized). Regression test added in test-fixes-sync.mjs. <!--id:FIX-465-->

The autonomous loop pushes these in tight bursts, so the heavy job spins up just to be cancelled by cancel-in-progress. Fix: move the cheap fixes-integrity guard (FIX-461) into its own .github/workflows/fixes-integrity.yml (no path filter — must fire on the docs-only commits it polices), and add paths-ignore: ['docs/**'] to tests.yml on.push + on.pull_request so the unit job skips docs-only changes (mixed docs+code commits still run it). Can't use a single workflow-level paths-ignore because that would also skip the guard on the exact docs-only done.log commits that are the FIX-461 failure mode. Caveat: if branch protection with required checks is later enabled, a paths-ignore-skipped workflow reports no status, so a required 'unit' check would block docs-only merges unless a skipped→success companion is added. <!--id:FIX-466-->

- [x] 🟡 S — **session:worktree:done leaves dir on disk when git worktree remove --force itself fails** — Distinct residual surfaced tearing down the [[FIX-477]]/[[FIX-479]] worktree: after [[FIX-479]] correctly auto-forces removal of a merged, porcelain-clean (artifact-only) tree, `git worktree remove --force` can ITSELF fail on a fully-installed worktree — a transient file lock on the freshly-built node_modules/.next (esbuild service, Defender scan) returns non-zero. git deregisters the worktree (it drops from `git worktree list`, .git pointer gone) but leaves the physical dir on disk, so done() dies after the unrecoverable remove and the dir strands (observed on the FIX-477 session: dir survived, `git worktree remove` then reported 'not a working tree'). core.longpaths=true is already set, so this is a lock/rmdir race, not the MAX_PATH limit. - [x] 🔴 S — **proposals introduced_at ORDER BY has no index -> full-sort timeout** — The PostgREST query behind the /proposals list (all+newest), the newest carousel, and the home-page fallback runs ORDER BY introduced_at DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT/OFFSET with no selective WHERE. There is no index on proposals(introduced_at) anywhere in migration history, so every request full-scans + sorts the whole proposals table; as the table grew this began hitting statement_timeout on prod. Fix: btree index on (introduced_at DESC NULLS LAST) to match the sort exactly (a backward scan of a default ASC index gives NULLS FIRST and won't match). Cross-ref [[FIX-444]] (prod gateway/timeout caps). <!--id:FIX-502-->
- [x] 🟡 M — **Pipeline buffer-churn: count→EXISTS, unindexed seq-scan counts, exact→estimated** — Pipeline-side buffer-churn (2026-06-06 audit; follow-up to [[FIX-503]]). (2) cron-run-postrun-extract + cron-run-anchor-verify run unindexed-source seq-scan count(*) per source — collapse into one GROUP BY RPC. (3) baseline-probe uses exact count where estimated (planner reltuples) is sufficient. These run against the cache-starved Pro Small and evict the request-path working set. Verify each fingerprint in pg_stat_statements before/after. <!--id:FIX-511-->

Durable fix so the temporary Vercel Firewall ClaudeBot challenge can later relax: robots.txt `Disallow: /*?` (param-free URLs stay crawlable); app/sitemap.ts (canonical bounded walk — ClaudeBot 404'd on /sitemap.xml; static pages + capped proposals/officials/institutions/jurisdictions, <=10k URLs, 5s per-query timeout, degrades to static-only); generateMetadata noindex,follow on any filtered/paginated /proposals view (bare stays indexable); page param clamped to [1,500]. - [x] 🟡 S — **20260420040000 fresh-replay fails: pg_trgm SCHEMA public vs extensions.gin_trgm_ops** — On a fresh local replay, 20260420040000_reconcile_prod_drift.sql declared `CREATE EXTENSION pg_trgm SCHEMA public` (line 15) while its trigram GIN index DDL references `extensions.gin_trgm_ops`, so replays failed with 'operator class extensions.gin_trgm_ops does not exist' (0001 lands pg_trgm in public). Replay-only in effect — prod has this migration recorded as applied and never re-runs it (`db:push:prod` won't touch it), so there is no prod-side change. Editing this one existing migration was explicitly authorized (2026-06-07). Surfaced after a Docker reinstall wiped the local data vhdx and forced a from-zero replay; see [[FIX-516]] for the broader replay-from-zero breakage. <!--id:FIX-515-->

- [x] 🟠 M — **Platform Costs egress: device-filter defect + honest NIC-proxy relabel** — The dashboard 'Database Egress' read 101% of the Pro 250 GB limit (~272 GB MTD). Root cause: egress is sourced from the Prometheus counter node_network_transmit_bytes_total (raw NIC transmit on ens5), an UPPER BOUND that includes replication, PITR/WAL, and intra-AWS traffic — NOT Supabase billable egress (bytes to clients). Two fixes: (1) parsePrometheusText summed ALL device= rows with no filter (latent — prod exposes only ens5 today, but lo/docker/veth/br/cni would inflate on other hosts); added labelExcludes to PromMatch and a NETWORK_VIRTUAL_DEVICES exclude list, plus a parser unit test. (2) Relabeled the metric honestly: snapshot writes egress with source='estimated' (gray '~ Est.' badge), platform_limits display_label → 'Egress (≈ NIC transmit, upper bound)', and computePlatformUsagePayload excludes source='estimated' rows from any_critical/any_warning so it no longer trips a false red banner. Investigation confirmed Supabase exposes NO public Management API endpoint for billable egress (api.supabase.com/v1 probed 2026-06-19: every egress variant 404s). Kill-switch wiring deferred — see [[FIX-603]]. <!--id:FIX-602-->

- [x] 🟠 S — **Harden FEC chunk upserts: retry+throw instead of silent failed-and-continue** — The FEC bulk indiv stage pre-upserts recipient-committee entities in 500-row chunks via PostgREST. The local FIX-677 backfill exposed a silent-partial bug: a chunk that timed out on transient IO/autovacuum contention was caught, logged, counted as `failed += chunk.length`, and skipped — 500 of 6,219 committees never entered `entityIdByCmte`, so their donors' donations were silently dropped downstream at `if (!toEntityId) continue;` while the donation-write count stayed green. Pro Small is more IO-bound, so this will recur during the prod backfill. Fix: wrap the per-chunk `.upsert()` in `upsertPacEntitiesBatch`, `upsertDonationRelationshipsBatch`, and `upsertIndependentExpendituresBatch` with retry-with-backoff (new `retryWithBackoff` in pipelines/utils.ts), then THROW on exhausted retries instead of counting-failed-and-continuing — aborting loudly lets the idempotent run be re-tried rather than shipping partial data. Adds an `indivCmteSkippedUnresolved` integrity counter to the indiv→committee build loop (should always read 0) so the backfill has a crisp done-gate. Excludes the direct-pg donor/indiv-to-committee writers and heavy-rebuild RPCs by design. Makes the prod FIX-677 backfill self-protecting. <!--id:FIX-686-->

- [x] 🟠 M — **pg_cron entity_connections rebuild dies at 2-min cluster statement_timeout** — The pg_cron `rebuild-ec-full` job ([[FIX-688]]) FAILED on its first scheduled firing (2026-06-29 08:00 UTC) after exactly 2 min: `canceling statement due to statement timeout` inside `rebuild_ec_donations_full_window`, called from `run_entity_connections_rebuild` ([[FIX-687]]). Root cause: the cluster-default `statement_timeout` is 2 min (`pg_settings.reset_val=120000ms`), inherited by the `postgres` role pg_cron runs as (the role sets no timeout of its own). The procedure body's `SET statement_timeout='90min'` and each chunk function's `proconfig` timeout (donations_full_window=45min) do NOT survive pg_cron's COMMIT-per-chunk execution: after the procedure's internal COMMITs the GUC reverts to the 2-min cluster default, so the first donations-window INSERT (needs tens of min) is killed at 2 min and the procedure aborts before its terminal data_sync_log UPDATE. Evidence: the `postgres` rolconfig holds only search_path (no statement_timeout); the OLD direct-pg TS path scripts/rebuild-entity-connections.ts (run-rebuild-chunks-prod) sets the timeout per-connection and completes fine (06-24 = 39.8 min / 2.59M edges) — so the rebuild logic is correct and only the pg_cron timeout inheritance is broken. Side effects of the abort: leaves entity_connections autovacuum_enabled=false (re-enable ALTER never reached; manually restored 2026-06-29) and a stuck `running` sync-log row (reaper self-heals). Candidate fixes (decide mechanism): (a) re-issue SET statement_timeout at the top of EACH loop iteration / after every COMMIT in the procedure (cheapest, targeted) and verify the per-chunk proconfig re-applies; (b) ALTER ROLE postgres IN DATABASE postgres SET statement_timeout — broad, and a role-level bump is risky per the cache-starvation notes; (c) set the timeout on the cron command string itself; (d) keep the rebuild on the proven GHA/TS direct-pg path and partially revert the FIX-688 pg_cron schedule. Until fixed, the twice-weekly graph rebuild is non-functional on prod and edges go stale (last good rebuild 2026-06-24). Surfaced by the FIX-677 prod backfill load-test (PR1 verification of FIX-687/688). <!--id:FIX-697-->
- [x] 🟠 M — **FEC JFC individual receipts double-counted + bloat 2024 indiv backfill past GHA 6h cap** — Two coupled findings from the FIX-677 prod backfill load-test (fec-backfill.yml run 28408664237, cancelled at 5h52m, incomplete). **(A) JFC individual-receipt double-count.** The non-candidate-committee recipient set `nonCandCmtes` in packages/data/src/pipelines/fec-bulk/index.ts is built from cm24 by **CMTE_TP only** (`NON_CAND_KEEP_TYPES = {O,X,Y,Z,N,Q,V,W}`); CMTE_DSGN (designation) is never parsed from cm24 (`CM_COL` has no CMTE_DSGN entry — `parseCm24` reads only CMTE_ID/CMTE_NM/CMTE_TP/CONNECTED_ORG_NM). The documented joint-fundraising/leadership exclusion (designation ∈ {J,D,B}) is applied ONLY on the ccl candidate-authorized path (indiv.ts `parseCcl`), NOT on the cm24/non-candidate path. So joint-fundraising committees filed as CMTE_TP='N' with CMTE_DSGN='J' — confirmed on prod: HARRIS VICTORY FUND (C00744946, tp=N, 339k rows/$837M), TRUMP 47 COMMITTEE (C00867937, tp=N, $341M), TRUMP NATIONAL COMMITTEE JFC (C00873893, tp=N, $146M), TRUMP SAVE AMERICA JFC (C00770941, tp=N, $70M) — slip through and are captured as individual→committee `donation` rows (source=fec_bulk_indiv_to_committee). JFC receipts are re-itemized to participants via JFC→participant transfers, so counting individual→JFC double-counts the same dollars (~$1.4B+ across those 4 JFCs alone). Fix: add CMTE_DSGN (cm24 col 8) to CM_COL + CommitteeInfo, and exclude CMTE_DSGN ∈ {J,D,B} when building nonCandCmtes — mirroring the ccl-path exclusion the header comment already claims. **(B) Full-cycle backfill exceeds the 6h GHA job cap.** The 2024 presidential indiv backfill wrote ~$3.42B / 1.59M indiv→committee rows + ~516k indiv→candidate over 5h52m at a ~30 rows/sec relationship-upsert rate on the Micro (vs ~490/sec for the donor-entity upsert — financial_relationships index maintenance is the per-row cost), and was cancelled before completing (UDP/super-PAC type-10 tail + Schedule-E IE + post-cycle recompute unfinished; UDP C00799031 = 0 rows). The pipeline has no checkpointing, so a re-dispatch restarts from zero and hits the same wall. Finding (A) removes ~600k+ rows of JFC volume and may bring a corrected run under the 6h budget; the per-row upsert speed (~30/s) still warrants benchmarking (chunk size / index maintenance on financial_relationships). The durable fix is watermark-resumable ingest (PR4 / [[FIX-689]] interim). **Until a clean run completes, total_received_cents / total_ie_*_cents must NOT be rebuilt** — the current prod state has partial + double-counted indiv→committee rows that are invisible only because the received-totals rebuild has not run. Surfaced by the supervised FIX-677 prod runbook (PR1 verification). Cross-ref [[FIX-677]] [[FIX-236]] [[FIX-689]]. <!--id:FIX-698-->

Three env knobs, each defaulting to current full-run behavior: FEC_INDIV_TX_TYPES (override the 15,15E,10 tx-type filter), FEC_INDIV_STAGES (comma allow-list of indiv sub-stages: donor-entities, indiv-to-candidate, recipient-entities, indiv-to-committee, independent-expenditures, totals), and the existing FEC_INDIV_CYCLES/FEC_CYCLES. - [x] 🟠 M — **FIX-698 over-excludes D (leadership) and B (SSF) designations from indiv-to-committee receipts** — Found during the [[FIX-677]] finish enumeration (cm24 parsed via the FIX-698 code path, joined to the prod 2024 fec_bulk_indiv_to_committee set). EXCLUDE_DESIGNATIONS in packages/data/src/pipelines/fec-bulk/index.ts is {J,D,B}, applied in buildNonCandRecipientSet to drop those designations from the individual-to-committee recipient set on a double-count rationale (they re-itemize receipts to participants via downstream transfers, so counting the individual-to-cmte leg double-counts). That rationale is airtight for J (joint-fundraising committees are legal conduits; the same dollars are transferred to participants who re-itemize them) but WRONG for B and shaky for D. B = Lobbyist/Registrant SSF PACs (e.g. NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF REALTORS PAC 6.6M, AIPAC PAC 5.7M, NATIONAL AUTOMOBILE DEALERS PAC 5.6M) and D = Leadership PACs (e.g. Trump NEVER SURRENDER INC 33M small-dollar) are ordinary contributing PACs: money comes in from members/donors, the PAC independently contributes to candidates. individual-to-PAC and PAC-to-candidate are two DISTINCT money legs, exactly like the type-N other-PACs and type-O super PACs FIX-698 KEEPS. No double-count. So excluding D and B drops legitimate direct individual receipts (2024 prod: 537 D cmtes / 69,800 rows / 82.9M, and 1,208 B cmtes / 162,532 rows / 287.6M). The FIX-677 finish DELETEd the D/B partial cancelled-run artifacts (they were essentially absent pre-run, baseline 42 rows, and inconsistent with current code) to keep prod consistent and restore status quo. Fix: narrow EXCLUDE_DESIGNATIONS to {J} only (keep D and B as valid recipients), extend jfc-exclusion.test.ts to assert D and B are KEPT (currently it asserts they are excluded), then a corrected complete indiv run backfills the D/B individual receipts. The complete-run cost is the same >6h GHA wall as [[FIX-698]](B) — durable path is watermark-resumable ingest [[FIX-689]]. Cross-ref [[FIX-698]] [[FIX-677]] [[FIX-236]]. <!--id:FIX-701-->
- [x] 🟠 M — **rebuild_financial_entity_donation_totals exceeds 90min on Micro (4M rows) — donor total_donated_cents chronically stale** — Surfaced during the [[FIX-677]] finish (fec-backfill run 28493948960, 2026-07-01). The totals stage logged `rebuild_financial_entity_donation_totals failed: canceling statement due to statement timeout` after running the full 90min (05:01->06:31 UTC). Root cause is NOT a missing override: the fn proconfig on prod IS statement_timeout=30min, but per packages/data/src/lib/heavy-rebuild.ts (header lines 12-14 + 124-125) statement_timeout is armed ONCE on the top-level statement using the SESSION value at statement start, so the function-level ALTER FUNCTION SET does NOT re-arm the outer SELECT rebuild_*() timer. runHeavyRebuild sets the session to 90min, so the effective cap is 90min. The rebuild itself (temp-table SUM of from_type=financial_entity + relationship_type=donation rows, now 4,056,034 rows = ~2x the ~2M it was tuned for at ~18min in 20260513010000) exceeded 90min on the cache-starved Micro (256MB shared_buffers / ~54pct hit, see [[FIX-503]]). Impact: (1) total_donated_cents is NOT refreshed, so it is chronically stale/understated on prod — this fires every fec-bulk run INCLUDING the nightly fec-phase, not just scoped runs; (2) worse on scoped runs (FIX-700 skips per-row aggregate overwrite, so the totals rebuild is the ONLY writer of donor outbound totals) — after the type-10 backfill the 92,982 type-10 donors show understated totals (e.g. ISENBERG $154,905 stored vs $197,522 live; PORTER $4,200 vs $10,700). Fixes: chunk the rebuild ([[FIX-263]] entity_connections pattern) or add a targeted variant that only re-sums entities with changed outbound (the interim remediation for the FIX-677 donors is a targeted UPDATE of the affected from_id set); durable path is chunked/resumable like the pg_cron entity_connections rebuild [[FIX-687]]. NOTE received-totals rebuild ([[FIX-269]] sibling) still succeeds (~56s, far fewer target rows) so super-PAC received data is fine. Cross-ref [[FIX-700]] [[FIX-269]] [[FIX-444]]. <!--id:FIX-702-->
- [x] 🔴 M — **pg_cron entity_connections FULL rebuild fails at 90min donations wall (no per-window COMMIT); statement_timeout also defeats chunk-failure resilience + strands autovacuum** — Surfaced by the [[FIX-677]] finish Phase 4 (the definitive prod proof of [[FIX-697]]). Scheduled a one-shot pg_cron CALL run_entity_connections_rebuild(full) at 06:57 UTC 2026-07-01. GOOD: it survived 90min with NO 2-min death, so FIX-697 (postgres-role statement_timeout=90min default surviving COMMITs) genuinely works. BAD: it FAILED at exactly 08:27:00 (=06:57+90min) in rebuild_ec_donations_full_window with canceling statement due to statement timeout (cron.job_run_details jobid 3). ROOT CAUSE: the procedure (supabase/migrations/20260628000100) runs the donations chunk = prepare()+16 windows+finalize() in ONE transaction with NO per-window COMMIT (intentional for rollback atomicity, lines 163-183). statement_timeout re-arms ONLY after a COMMIT; the last COMMIT before the chunk was the autovacuum-pause at line 124 (~run start), so the ENTIRE donations chunk shares ONE 90min budget. The code comment at lines 164-166 claiming each window gets its own fresh statement_timeout is FALSE (that only holds if a COMMIT separates them, as the OLD TS direct-pg path did via autocommit-per-window). Post-FIX-677 the donation edge set grew (America PAC ~93k donor edges, plus all type-10 super-PAC donors) so the chunk now exceeds 90min on the cache-starved Micro ([[FIX-503]]); the last good full rebuild was 39.8min on 06-24 (pre-FIX-677, TS path). SECONDARY BUG: the per-chunk EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS resilience (lines 191-196) is DEFEATED by statement_timeout — once the timer expires, every subsequent statement (the COMMIT, other chunks, the terminal UPDATE) instantly re-times-out, so the procedure aborts entirely and NEVER writes its terminal failed row: the data_sync_log row was stranded running (had to hand-mark failed), the whole run rolled back (edges unchanged at 2,790,628), and entity_connections autovacuum was left stranded OFF (line-207 re-enable never reached — the recurring [[FIX-590]] hazard; cleaned up manually). FIXES: (a) COMMIT after each donations window to restore the TS autocommit-per-window semantics so each window gets a fresh 90min timer (trades all-or-nothing atomicity for resumability — acceptable, matches historical TS behavior, next rebuild re-runs), or use finer windows (32/64) each well under 90min; (b) in the failure path reset statement_timeout before the terminal UPDATE + autovacuum re-enable so cleanup always runs (or move them to a guaranteed path); (c) fix the misleading comment. IMPACT: [[FIX-687]]/[[FIX-688]] pg_cron FULL rebuild does NOT complete on prod — the Mon rebuild-ec-full job would fail every week at this wall; graph donation edges cannot refresh via pg_cron. Both jobs remain paused. Interim reconciliation path = the TS direct-pg rebuild (per-window autocommit). Cross-ref [[FIX-697]] [[FIX-687]] [[FIX-688]] [[FIX-291]] [[FIX-590]]. <!--id:FIX-703-->
- [x] 🔴 M — **pg_cron full rebuild tail wedges Micro: finalize stale-VM 4h + donor-rollup MV REFRESH CONCURRENTLY OOM** — Surfaced by the [[FIX-703]] supervised prod full rebuild (2026-07-02). [[FIX-703]] fixed the donations windows (per-window COMMIT + postgres role-default statement_timeout 90min->6h; the CALL-start timer is immutable inside a CALLed procedure so per-COMMIT/in-proc-SET/proconfig can't re-arm it — only the role default works). The donation/super-PAC edges DID land (edges 2,790,628 -> 4,794,034; donation 1,682,742 -> 3,686,148, closing [[FIX-677]] Phase 4). BUT the rebuild's TAIL wedged prod and the run died at the 6h CALL wall, then the MV step OOM-wedged Micro (had to restart compute via Management API). Two durable problems, both re-triggered by every scheduled full run (rebuild-ec-full Mon 08:00) so BOTH jobs remain PAUSED until fixed: (1) FINALIZE (rebuild_ec_donations_full_finalize recipient_count UPDATE) runs while autovacuum is PAUSED (FIX-590) right after the 16 windows delete+insert all ~3.69M donation edges — the newly-written pages aren't all-visible so its Index Only Scan on entity_connections_from_type_from_id_to_type_to_id_connecti_key degrades to per-row heap fetches -> ~4h on the doubled edge set (with a FRESH vacuum it was 33min; measured). A single non-committable statement, so per-window COMMIT can't help. Fix options: re-enable autovacuum + VACUUM entity_connections BEFORE finalize (VACUUM can't run inside the procedure -> move finalize to a separate pg_cron step after a vacuum, or drop the FIX-590 autovacuum pause, or make finalize incremental/cheaper). (2) REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY official_donor_rollup_mv builds a full second copy of the doubled donor set -> OOM'd Micro so hard NO new connection (pooler session+txn ECHECKOUTTIMEOUT, Management API 544, econnrefused) could be established; app served stale/edge-cache only; required a compute restart. On restart the killed refresh rolled back so the MV kept its PRIOR snapshot (currently STALE — missing the new super-PAC donor money). Fix options: non-CONCURRENT REFRESH (lighter memory, faster, but ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on the MV during refresh — acceptable off-peak), or bound work_mem/maintenance_work_mem for the refresh, or upgrade compute, or make the rollup incremental. INTERIM STATE: donation edges + recipient_count fresh & committed; donor-rollup MV stale (needs a controlled off-peak refresh); jobs paused; interim reconcile still via the TS direct-pg path. - [x] 🟠 S — **Scoped FEC indiv re-runs are no-op'd by the FIX-193 Last-Modified watermark** — A scoped FEC bulk run (FEC_INDIV_TX_TYPES / FEC_INDIV_STAGES / FEC_INDIV_RECIPIENT_CMTES set) is an explicit surgical re-ingest, but the FIX-193 indiv watermark short-circuit skips the entire indiv stage when FEC's indiv{yy}.zip Last-Modified is unchanged since the last run. A CLOSED cycle's indiv file never changes again, so ANY scoped re-run of a closed cycle is silently no-op'd — the [[FIX-701]] 2024 D/B re-capture dispatch hit exactly this (indiv stage skipped → zero D/B rows restored; only the unrelated Schedule-E stage ran). - [x] 🟠 S — **runFecBulkPipeline exits 0 on a caught fatal — GHA marks a failed run 'success'** — runFecBulkPipeline() catches its own fatal errors, calls failSync(), and RETURNS a result object instead of rethrowing; the standalone entrypoint then does `.then(() => process.exit(0))` unconditionally. So a pipeline that dies mid-run (e.g. a financial_entities chunk hitting the prod statement_timeout) logs 'FEC bulk pipeline fatal error: …', writes a failed data_sync_log row, and STILL exits 0 → the GHA step (fec-backfill.yml / nightly fec-phase) shows green. Surfaced during the [[FIX-701]] re-capture: a run that failed at the pas2 upsert reported conclusion=success and I only caught it by reading the log. The Mark-killed backstop only covers SIGTERM/timeout kills, not caught fatals. Fix: the entrypoint should inspect the PipelineResult (or the pipeline should rethrow) and process.exit(1) when the run failed / failSync fired, so CI status is trustworthy. Keep the graceful cleanup, just exit nonzero on failure. <!--id:FIX-727-->

The WEEKLY `financial-entity-totals-incremental` is live+correct and is the durable path; the monthly is only the hard-delete orphan safety net (rare), so this is not urgent. - [x] 🟠 L — **fec_bulk indiv ingest: checkpoint/resume across nightly runs (PR4)** — The nightly fec-phase job SIGTERMs at its 150-min budget on heavy Sundays (GHA 28755577316: donor-entities upsert 52m + indiv-to-candidate 47m + indiv-to-committee killed 32m in = 88% of wall; download+extract+stream is only ~2.3m / ~1.5%). On resume, re-download (R2 cache) + re-stream rebuilds the in-RAM maps deterministically; completed upsert stages rebuild their id maps via batched direct-pg reads instead of re-running; a stored-total mismatch resets that stage's cursor to 0 (idempotent). Scoped runs ([[FIX-700]]/[[FIX-701]]) bypass the machinery entirely; [[FIX-193]] watermark semantics unchanged (advance only on full completion, then state cleared). Confirmed on the supervised 2026-07-08 run 28911039672: BOTH categories read EXACTLY 1,000,000 rows (contracts 823,083 upserted, assistance 68,932 upserted, 0 failed) — a truncation tell; a range-read of the two zips central directories showed FY2026_All_Contracts_Full = 3 CSV parts and FY2026_All_Assistance_Full = 4 parts. So prod holds only ~1/3 of contract awards and ~1/4 of the assistance scan (the majority of grant-shaped awards in parts 2-4 are lost). Latent since inception — every prior successful run (April/May) also processed part 1 only; the job reports success because each part-1 stream completes cleanly and nothing signals the dropped parts. Fix: enumerate ALL .csv entries in extractCsvFromZip (extract each to its own path, run processCsvFile over each, accumulate FileResult), or concatenate parts while stripping the per-part header. Each part carries its own header row so columns:true parsing works per-file unchanged. Cost: a full run then processes ~3M contracts + ~4M assistance rows, roughly 3-4x wall-clock (~90 min, still inside the 350-min cap) and ~3x prod write volume — run at low-traffic hours. Complements checkpoint/resume [[FIX-739]] and the manual-workflow split [[FIX-740]]; independent of the direct-pg timeout fix [[FIX-586]]. Secondary: .usaspending-bulk-state.json is gitignored and runners are ephemeral, so every CI dispatch logs No prior state first run and always runs Full (delta path dead in CI) — folds into [[FIX-739]]. <!--id:FIX-766-->

- [x] 🔴 M — **Invert CDN cache model: page allowlist in config, API handlers own their cache headers** — Follow-on to [[FIX-795]]: the denylist model fails unsafe — every new per-user route is a latent [[FIX-786]] cross-user cache leak until someone remembers to denylist it, and config headers() rules are method- and status-blind (captured live: cdnHot stamped on POST /api/comments/[id]/rate responses and on a 429 RSC response). Invert: the catch-all dies; cdnHot applies ONLY to an explicit allowlist of viewer-independent public PAGE prefixes; unlisted routes get nothing stamped (Next's own private/no-store for dynamic routes then stands) — a new route is safe by default, forgetting to list it costs performance never correctness. API routes own their cache headers in code ([[FIX-787]]/[[FIX-788]] pattern): the public-API cdnHot stamps (statements, questions, browse, typeahead, positions/rollup, summaries) move into the handlers where they can be GET-only and 200-only. Rule made structural: cache headers only on payloads with zero viewer-dependence, set as close to the response as possible. <!--id:FIX-796-->
- [x] 🟠 S — **Router prefetches drain the entity_leaf rate-limit cap — a single browser 429s itself** — Captured on prod: link-dense pages (e.g. the USA jurisdiction page) fire dozens of Next.js router prefetches (Next-Router-Prefetch: 1 RSC GETs) that drain the [[FIX-683]] entity_leaf Upstash cap (45/min) — one human's browser 429s itself (retry-after: 45, x-ratelimit-remaining: 0). Fix: separate bucket, not exemption — requests carrying the prefetch header count against their own generous bucket (~300/min) instead of the entity_leaf/entity_pages caps; real navigations keep the existing caps. Spoofing the header just moves a crawler to a different capped bucket — no bypass. Also: the middleware 429 must carry explicit no-store cache headers so a rate-limited response can never be edge-cached and served to other users (the [[FIX-796]] status-blind stamp landed on a 429 in the captures). <!--id:FIX-797-->

Follows C0 [[FIX-519]] substrate. <!--id:FIX-523-->

- [x] 🟠 S — **Middleware writes rotated auth cookies to response only — post-then-get flows can read as anon (FIX-784 root cause)** — The auth-refresh block in apps/civitics/middleware.ts writes Supabase's rotated session cookies to the RESPONSE only (response.cookies.set), not to the forwarded request. This deviates from the canonical @supabase/ssr Next.js pattern, which also does request.cookies.set + rebuilds NextResponse.next({request}) so the refreshed session reaches route handlers / server components in the SAME request. Consequence: when the access token is expired and middleware refreshes it (rotating + consuming the old refresh token), the handler re-reads the pre-rotation cookie, its getUser() falls back to the already-consumed refresh token, and it authenticates as ANON. This is the root cause behind [[FIX-784]] (saved views: the post-save reload GET that lost the rotation race read anon → empty-200 → wiped list). FIX-784 made saved-views immune by broadcasting deltas instead of re-fetching, but the middleware bug is latent for ANY post-then-get / rapid-successive authed flow. Fix: adopt the canonical request+response cookie write in setAll. References [[FIX-784]]. <!--id:FIX-785-->

[packages/data/src/pipelines/fec-bulk/indiv.ts](../packages/data/src/pipelines/fec-bulk/indiv.ts) `normalizeName()` replaces every non-alphanumeric (including apostrophes) with whitespace, then collapses runs of whitespace. Surnames like `O'BRIEN`, `D'ANGELO`, `M'CARTHY` tokenize as `O BRIEN` / `D ANGELO` / `M CARTHY`, so `first_token` becomes `O` / `D` / `M` instead of the real surname. ~5,000 individual donor rows affected with spurious leading tokens: `O` (2,965 rows), `DE` (933), `D` (403), `ST` (265), `MC` (181), `M` (176). Fix: replace apostrophes (and periods) with **empty string** (NOT whitespace) before the non-alphanumeric replacement step, so `O'BRIEN` → `OBRIEN` and `M.D.` → `MD`. Two downstream constraints reject these batches wholesale: (a) [supabase/migrations/20260510000008_irs990.sql:127](../supabase/migrations/20260510000008_irs990.sql#L127) `irs990_grants_out` UNIQUE(filing_id, recipient_name_canonical, amount_cents) — when two grant lines share canonical recipient + amount, [packages/data/src/pipelines/irs990/writer.ts:351-383](../packages/data/src/pipelines/irs990/writer.ts#L351-L383) `upsertGrantsOutBatch`'s single-statement `.upsert(..., {onConflict})` fails with `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE command cannot affect row a second time`, dropping the entire batch; (b) [supabase/migrations/20260423000000_financial_relationships_donation_unique.sql:20](../supabase/migrations/20260423000000_financial_relationships_donation_unique.sql#L20) `financial_relationships_relcycle_unique(relationship_type, from_id, to_id, cycle_year)` — when two grants to the same recipient have the same cycle_year (any amount), [packages/data/src/pipelines/irs990/writer.ts:407-465](../packages/data/src/pipelines/irs990/writer.ts#L407-L465) `writeGrantRelationships`'s `.insert(rows)` collides regardless of amount. Concrete impact from the 2026-05-14 local re-run: AMERICAN MEDICAL ASSOCIATION 2025 filing lost 142 grants_out rows + 25 financial_relationships rows; smaller losses elsewhere across the seed set (199 failures total). Action: in both writer paths, aggregate by (filing_id, recipient_name_canonical) for `irs990_grants_out` and by (filing_object_id, toEntityId, taxYear) for `financial_relationships` BEFORE the upsert/insert — sum amount_cents, preserve count in metadata, keep first purpose (or concat unique purposes if cheap). Mirrors the FEC PAC pipeline's per-(committee × candidate × cycle) aggregation pattern. No schema change needed — the aggregation is application-layer; the UNIQUE keys are correct for the aggregated shape. Out of scope for FIX-277 because the bug pre-dates Session 1 and the local-only runtime confirmation surfaced after the patch landed; queuing as a separate fix to keep the FIX-277 commit narrow. <!--id:FIX-279-->

Two things bundled into one commit because the second blocks the first. **(1) RPC bugfix.** Session 1's `resolve_entity_by_canonical` (migration `20260514000000`) used `SELECT count(*), max(id) INTO v_count, v_id FROM public.financial_entities …` to detect single-match. Postgres 17.6 has no `max(uuid)` aggregate, so the function threw `function max(uuid) does not exist` on every match and never returned a non-NULL UUID. Session 2's IRS 990 + EDGAR patches (FIX-277/278) gracefully degraded to INSERT-everything on RPC error so the bug was silent — but the patches haven't actually prevented any cross-source duplicates since they shipped on 2026-05-15. New migration [supabase/migrations/20260517000000_fix_resolve_entity_by_canonical_max_uuid.sql](../supabase/migrations/20260517000000_fix_resolve_entity_by_canonical_max_uuid.sql) replaces the count+max trick with a `LIMIT 2 + array_agg + array_length` pattern that's UUID-safe; signature, return type, and contract unchanged. **(2) LittleSis hop-1 patch.** [packages/data/src/pipelines/littlesis/writer.ts](../packages/data/src/pipelines/littlesis/writer.ts) `upsertHop1FinancialEntities` previously did a bare INSERT per chunk of 500 entities, applying a `[LS:<id>]` suffix to individual canonical_names. New helper `resolveOrInsertHop1` calls `resolve_entity_by_canonical` first — single-match → bind via `external_source_refs` instead of INSERTing a duplicate; NULL → fall through to INSERT under the base canonical. Persons use `p_entity_type='individual'` (RPC's `donor_fingerprint IS NOT NULL` filter excludes LS-only individuals from accidental cross-pollution under common names); orgs use `p_entity_type=NULL` to allow LS 'corporation'/'other' to bind to existing 'nonprofit'/'corporation'/'other' rows under the same canonical (Heritage Foundation case per investigation §5.6), mirroring Session 2's IRS 990 pattern. `[LS:<id>]` suffix code removed — match-first via RPC supersedes its collision-prevention purpose, and 0 of 84,811 production LS-bound individuals carried it pre-patch (investigation §9 OOS #1). Caller [packages/data/src/pipelines/littlesis/index.ts](../packages/data/src/pipelines/littlesis/index.ts) log line gains `matched=` and `rpcErrors=` counters for observability; binding metadata stamps `confidence='canonical_match'` for RPC-resolved bindings vs `'hop1'` for new inserts. Bounded concurrency `RESOLVE_BATCH=50` replaces the prior 500-row INSERT chunk (the RPC + INSERT path is per-row and parallelizes naturally). Idempotency for previously-bound LS ids stays upstream via `preloadKnownLittleSisIds` + `if (known.has(lsId)) continue` at index.ts:154 — no LS id reaches the new helper after a successful prior binding, so the IRS 990 Stage 1 `external_source_refs` pre-check is unnecessary here. No prod backfill — forward-looking. **Local result (2026-05-17 re-run):** `inserted=119,275 matched=19,660 failed=0 rpcErrors=0` — 19,660 cross-source duplicates prevented in a single run. Anchor cases: ELON MUSK / ELON MUSK REVOCABLE TRUST / THOMAS PETERFFY each 1 row (unchanged). Multi-FEC residue stays as expected for FIX-239 Layer 2 (JOHN ARNOLD 14→16, M JUDE REYES 3→4, PAUL SINGER 6→7 — RPC returns NULL on multi-match per single-match-only contract, falls through to INSERT). 0 rows with `[LS:]` suffix post-patch. RPC smoke-test post-fix: PETERFFY single-match returns UUID, SINGER multi-match returns NULL, missing canonical returns NULL, empty returns NULL. **Verified local** — prod verification deferred to 2026-05-17 Sunday cron (also retroactively unblocks FIX-277 + FIX-278 on Pro). <!--id:FIX-280-->

Block 10 of `rebuild_entity_connections()` materializes both. Matcher rule (conservative — Craig's explicit answer): exact `normalizeName(officer.full_name) == normalize(donor.display_name)` AND `canonicalizeEntityName(donor.metadata->>'employer') == company.canonical_name`. Probes BOTH name orderings (FIRST-LAST and LAST-FIRST) because FEC stores `donor_fingerprint` as `LAST FIRST|ZIP` while EDGAR officer rosters are FIRST LAST — until FIX-238 reorders donor canonical the matcher has to bridge. Weaker matches (name-only, no employer match) → `external_relationships_review_queue` with `reason='name_match_no_employer'`; `too_many_lastname_hits` mirrors LittleSis. Review queue uses `source_relationship_id = source_entity_id` (not NULL) so re-runs are idempotent under the UNIQUE(source, source_entity_id, source_relationship_id) constraint. Person-shareholder matching uses the same rule; org-shareholder matching is deferred (queue reason `'org_holder_unmatched'`). Two scripts: `pnpm data:edgar` (weekly Sunday DEF 14A reconciliation), `pnpm data:edgar:daily` (daily 13D/G poll against the SEC daily full-index). SEC fair-access: `client.ts` enforces the required `"Civitics Platform civitics.platform@gmail.com"` User-Agent and a sliding-window 10 req/sec ceiling across all stages. New TS dep: `node-html-parser`. Exports `normalizeName` from `fec-bulk/indiv.ts` so EDGAR can match on the donor-side fingerprint canonical without forking. Wired into nightly orchestrator after LittleSis. **Anchor-batch result (5 CIKs, prod):** Apple's DEF 14A SCT parses cleanly (5/5 NEOs); Luca Maestri auto-links to his Apple-employer FEC donor row; Tim Cook + Kate Adams route to the review queue (same name + different employer — likely different people, conservative threshold did its job). JPMorgan / Lockheed / Pfizer / Disney use multi-table SCT layouts the V1 single-table heuristic doesn't catch — log+skip with `unparseable=4/5`. Parser improvements (multi-table SCT, name-only-cell + title-only-cell layouts, 10-K fallback, R1000 universe, 13F) are follow-up FIXes; coverage will improve incrementally. Verified local + prod. <!--id:FIX-253-->

The 60 leftover rows are written without a real apostrophe: `O BRIEN, MICHAEL` (space-separated), `O' BRIEN, JAMES` (apostrophe + space), `` O`BRIEN, HALLEY MARIE `` (backtick instead of apostrophe). FIX-239 Layer 1 can't see those as a single token; would need either (a) backtick added to the `['.]` strip set, plus (b) recognition of the leading `O `/`D `/`DE `/`ST `/`MC ` particle pattern that joins those tokens to the next when followed by uppercase ASCII. Keep narrow: only join when the leading token is exactly `O`, `D`, `DE`, `ST`, `MC` AND the surname is at position 0 (before the comma). ### DASHBOARD

- [x] 🔴 S — **Dashboard admin-content leaks via Vercel edge cache** — `/dashboard` is edge-cached for 30 min (`next.config.mjs` `cdnHot(1800, 3600)` rule). Vercel doesn't vary on cookies, so any admin-rendered SSR HTML — `KillSwitchBanner` events, the `ManualMetricsPanel` rows (separately removed by [[FIX-348]]) — gets cached and served to subsequent anonymous visitors for the cache lifetime. Symmetric leak in reverse: anon HTML cached → admin sees stripped page until expiry. Surfaced 2026-05-24 when admin content rendered for Craig in dev despite the dev cookies path having no edge cache (a stale Supabase refresh-token cookie made `getUser()` resolve to admin even when not signed in). Also surfaced two broken admin gates in scope: `window.CIVITICS_ADMIN` was read in 3 places (`PlatformCostsSection.tsx:58`, `ModerationSection.tsx:9`, `ManualMetricsPanel.tsx:18`) but set nowhere, so the per-metric Verify/Update buttons and the entire ModerationSection had been silently dead. Fix: SSR HTML carries no admin-only content; `KillSwitchBanner` becomes self-fetching client-side (drops the `events` prop, GETs `/api/admin/kill-switches/recent` on mount); new `/api/admin/me` cookie-based gate route + shared `useIsAdmin()` hook in `apps/civitics/src/lib/use-is-admin.ts` replaces the three inline broken hooks; `dashboard/page.tsx` drops `cookies()` + `createServerClient` + `getRecentKillSwitchEvents` + `getManualMetrics`. Each admin API route 404s for non-admins so admin content never reaches the wire. <!--id:FIX-347-->

The egress metric the panel exposed will autopopulate once Supabase Prometheus integration lands (separate forthcoming PR), eliminating the last meaningful manual entry. Delete `apps/civitics/app/dashboard/ManualMetricsPanel.tsx` and `apps/civitics/app/api/admin/usage-update/route.ts` (sole caller); the other admin update path (`/api/platform/usage` POST with `X-Admin-Key`) stays. `platform_usage.stale_after_days = 14` on the egress row stays for `SourceDisplay`'s isStale logic. <!--id:FIX-348-->
- [x] 🟠 M — **Data Health card cadence + alias + window fixes** — The dashboard Data Health card on /dashboard?tab=operations diverges from /admin/pipeline-health in three load-bearing ways. Surfacing case: TIGER Districts last ran 16 days ago. /admin/pipeline-health shows it correctly (within the 30-day MV window). Data Health reads `pending / never` because (1) [getPipelines()](../apps/civitics/app/api/claude/status/_lib/sections.ts) pulled `data_sync_log ORDER BY completed_at DESC LIMIT 100` so high-frequency writers (ai_summaries, tag_ai, tag_rules, regulations, congress_officials) monopolised the window and pushed annual-cadence pipelines like `tiger_districts` out; (2) [pipelineFreshness()](../apps/civitics/app/dashboard/DashboardClient.tsx) hard-coded a 48h ok / 168h warning threshold, so TIGER (annual by design) returned `error` past 7 days even when healthy; (3) [DataHealthSection](../apps/civitics/app/dashboard/DashboardClient.tsx)'s multi-alias rollup (Congress = officials + votes + committees) flatMap'd alias history into one merged list and lost per-alias identity, so the row badge went green if *any* alias completed in 48h — masking a stale or failing sub-pipeline. Three bundled sub-fixes: (a) add `cadence` field to `PipelineDef` (hourly/daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly/annual/on_demand/continuous) and refactor freshness to cadence-aware thresholds; right-column timestamp prefixes `Current · ` on healthy slow-cadence rows so 16d-old TIGER reads as healthy at-a-glance. (b) replace global LIMIT 100 with (pipeline ASC, completed_at DESC) + 14-month window + 3000-row safety limit + JS-side per-pipeline bucketing so every registered pipeline with a run in window appears reliably. (c) worst-status alias rollup — Congress.gov row reads red when any of {congress_officials, congress_votes, congress_committees, congress} is stale or failing; expanded panel adds per-alias sub-pipeline breakdown with ← propagating marker on the alias that drove the verdict. Adjustments from initial proposal: `courtlistener` daily→weekly (CLAUDE.md confirms weekly via Sunday block); `legistar` weekly→on_demand (CLAUDE.md: "Manual only"); `usaspending` monthly→weekly + dropped legacy `usaspending` alias (FIX-249 deprecation shipped); `ai_summaries` + `tag_ai` continuous→on_demand (work moved to enrichment_queue subagent drain, no longer writes data_sync_log). <!--id:FIX-382-->

- [x] 🟠 S — **Raise nightly `NODE_OPTIONS` to `--max-old-space-size=12288`** — The 2026-05-12 cron OOM'd mid-stream on the 2024 FEC indiv stage at the 8 GB V8 ceiling. `packages/data/CLAUDE.md` already documents 12 GB for presidential cycles (2024/2028); the workflow was lagging the guidance. ubuntu-latest runners ship 16 GB so 12 GB still leaves real headroom. - [x] 🟠 S — **Stranded `data_sync_log status='running'` rows on OOM/SIGTERM** — When Node aborts uncatchably (V8 OOM = SIGABRT, SIGKILL, hard crash) the in-flight pipeline never reaches `completeSync()`/`failSync()` and its row strands in `status='running'` forever, polluting `data:status` and the Data Freshness dashboard (one such row was left behind by the 2026-05-12 cron). Two-layer fix: (a) process-level signal handler in [packages/data/src/pipelines/sync-log.ts](../packages/data/src/pipelines/sync-log.ts) tracks in-flight log ids and best-effort `failSync(id, 'node-aborted-{signal}')` on SIGTERM / SIGINT / SIGHUP / uncaughtException / unhandledRejection (2s budget, then exit); (b) new `reap_stale_sync_log(stale_minutes)` RPC ([migration 20260512100000](../supabase/migrations/20260512100000_reap_stale_sync_log.sql)) flips rows older than threshold to `failed` with `error_message='reaped_orphan'`, idempotent, called from `runNightlySync` entry + standalone `pnpm data:reap-sync-log`. V8 OOM (SIGABRT) and SIGKILL are uncatchable from JS — the reaper RPC is the only recovery for those cases (documented inline). See `docs/audits/cron_run_2026-05-12.md` §10/§11. <!--id:FIX-255-->
- [x] 🔴 L — **Chunked `rebuild_entity_connections()` by connection_type** — Post-FIX-236, financial_relationships holds 4.1M donations + 1.3M contracts + 88K grants + IE rows. The monolithic TRUNCATE+rebuild exceeded the 20-min outer session statement_timeout twice in the 2026-05-13 audit Run #2, leaving entity_connections frozen at 1,914,433 rows (FIX-236 donations not in the graph). Split into 10 per-connection-type functions ([migration 20260513000000](../supabase/migrations/20260513000000_chunked_rebuild_entity_connections.sql)) — `_donations` (60min timeout, ~4M edges, includes ie_support fold-in + recipient_count update), `_votes`, `_cosponsors`, `_appointments`, `_oversight`, `_holds`, `_gifts`, `_contracts` (30min, ~1.3M), `_lobbying`, `_external` (runs last, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING for LittleSis overlap). Orchestrator at [packages/data/src/pipelines/index.ts:816](../packages/data/src/pipelines/index.ts#L816) calls each chunk as a separate top-level statement with statement_timeout reset to 45min between calls — each chunk gets a fresh wall-clock budget. Per-chunk DELETE replaces the global TRUNCATE, so live reads on /officials/[id] and /donors/[id] are no longer blocked by an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the entire rebuild window. Partial failure isolation: if one chunk times out, subsequent chunks continue. Umbrella `rebuild_entity_connections()` preserved for PostgREST local-dev callers. **Prod result:** 4,577,596 edges in 71.97min (donation 60min/3.85M, votes 8min/481K, contracts 40s/61K, external 3.4min/183K). Verified local + prod. See `docs/audits/cron_run_2026-05-12.md` §11. <!--id:FIX-263-->

- [x] 🔴 M — **Live Cloudflare R2 metrics in platform_usage via GraphQL Analytics** — Cloudflare rows in `platform_usage` (`storage_bytes`, `class_a_ops`, `class_b_ops`) sat at manually-entered values from 2026-03-24 (7+ weeks stale) because PR 1's snapshot only knew how to call Supabase + Anthropic. Per-bucket detail returned in `buckets: Record<string, {...}>` so a future per-bucket dashboard tab is unblocked without re-instrumenting; PR 2 only writes the aggregate `totals` to `platform_usage`. 5-min in-memory cache mirrors `getSupabaseManagementMetrics`; missing env returns `{error}` so the snapshot keeps producing rows. New debug route `/api/platform/cloudflare` exposes the raw helper output (GET) and clears the cache (POST + `X-Admin-Key`). Wired into `computePlatformUsagePayload` alongside Supabase. After deploy, all three Cloudflare rows flip from `source='manual'` → `source='api'` on the first cron tick. Token + account ID already in `.env.example`; must be added to Vercel prod env before deploy. PR 2 of 3 (platform monitoring overhaul). <!--id:FIX-283-->

- [x] 🟠 M — **Live GitHub Actions usage in platform_usage (enhanced billing API)** — GHA is now part of the operational stack (platform-snapshot every 10 min plus the existing nightly/audit/sync-canary workflows) but no metric was captured for it. Civitics is a public repo so Actions minutes are unlimited and *not* a cost-protection lever today; the work is (a) storage tracking — Actions cache + artifacts ARE billed on public repos above 500 MB, (b) future-proofing — if the repo ever flips private (early-access, sensitive forks) the 10-min platform-snapshot cron alone is ~4,320 billed minutes/month, over double the free 2,000 cap, (c) operational visibility alongside the other vendors. **Two premise corrections from the prompt:** (1) `civitics-platform` is a USER account, not an org (confirmed via `/user` returning login=civitics-platform with no `/user/orgs` membership) — org-level endpoints `/orgs/{org}/settings/billing/*` 404. (2) The legacy user-level `/settings/billing/actions` + `/settings/billing/shared-storage` endpoints return **HTTP 410 "This endpoint has been moved"** as of May 2026 — GitHub sunset both in favor of the unified enhanced-billing endpoint `/users/{user}/settings/billing/usage[?year=YYYY&month=MM]`. Helper [packages/db/src/github-usage.ts](../packages/db/src/github-usage.ts) hits the enhanced endpoint scoped to the current calendar month and aggregates the line-item `usageItems` array (each item has `product`, `sku`, `quantity`, `unitType`, `pricePerUnit`, `grossAmount`, `discountAmount`, `netAmount`). Returns `action_minutes` (sum of `quantity` where `unitType='Minutes'`), `minutes_breakdown` (per-SKU rollup — `{"Actions Linux": 593}` for civitics today; populated automatically if macOS/Windows runners are ever added), `storage_bytes` (best-effort across `product IN ('shared_storage','packages')` — `GigabyteHours` converted to "average bytes over the period so far" via `gbh / hours_elapsed * 1024³`; civitics currently has zero storage line items so this resolves to 0), plus `total_billed_usd` + `total_gross_usd` for completeness. Account path hardcoded as `users/civitics-platform`; swap to `orgs/<slug>` if the repo is ever transferred to a real GitHub Org (endpoint shape is identical). 5-min in-memory cache mirrors Cloudflare/Vercel helpers; failure → `{error}` keeps the snapshot's "data is fresh OR stale, never half-fresh" rule intact. New migration [20260517030000_github_platform_limits.sql](../supabase/migrations/20260517030000_github_platform_limits.sql) seeds two rows: `action_minutes` (plan='free', included_limit=-1 → unlimited per Vercel Pro `function_invocations` pattern at [0024:141](../supabase/migrations/0024_platform_usage_tracking.sql#L141), informational only) and `storage_bytes` (included_limit=500 MB, overage 0.008 per_gb). **Inline-documented caveat:** GitHub charges $0.008/GB/**DAY** for storage — only vendor in the model billed daily not monthly. Downstream overage math treats `overage_unit_cost` as $/(unit) without cadence knowledge, so any future displayed storage overage cost will under-report by ~30× until the evaluator learns about per-day cadence (PR 3 / future FIX). Wired into [computePlatformUsagePayload](../packages/db/src/platform-snapshot.ts) after the Cloudflare branch. New debug route `/api/platform/github` mirrors the Cloudflare shape (GET = raw helper output incl. per-SKU minutes breakdown + USD totals, POST + `X-Admin-Key` = clear cache). New env var `GITHUB_BILLING_TOKEN` (fine-grained PAT owned by `civitics-platform` with account-permission `Plan: Read`; classic PAT with `user` scope also works — existing `GITHUB_TOKEN` has only `read:org, repo`, returns 403 on billing endpoints, confirmed) added to [.env.example](../.env.example) and [turbo.json](../turbo.json) passthrough. Missing token is treated as benign (matches FIX-284 convention — does NOT trip `partial: true`); rows stay on `source='manual'` until token is added. PR 2.5 of 3 (platform monitoring overhaul); per-workflow breakdown + workflow failure rate are explicitly out of scope (would require iterating `/repos/.../actions/runs` — file a follow-up FIX when needed). <!--id:FIX-285-->

Prometheus exposes `node_cpu_seconds_total{cpu="<n>",mode="<idle|user|system|iowait|...>"}` as a per-core monotonic counter. **Shape:** new `applyTickDelta()` helper in [packages/db/src/supabase-prometheus.ts](../packages/db/src/supabase-prometheus.ts) — same `supabase_prometheus_state` table FIX-349 introduced, but returns `current - last_raw` (per-tick delta) instead of `current - baseline` (month-to-date) since CPU has no monthly accumulator semantic. Counter-reset detection (`current < last`) on node restart sets both fields to current + returns 0, avoiding wild ticks. Helper walks every `node_cpu_seconds_total{...}` line, accumulates `busy_delta` (sum where `mode != 'idle'`) and `total_delta` (sum over all modes + cores), computes `cpu_pct = 100 * busy_delta / total_delta` — num_cores divides out of both so the formula is robust across compute-tier upgrades. Two new state rows seeded on first tick (`cpu_busy_seconds_total`, `cpu_total_seconds_total`). New `platform_limits` row `(supabase, cpu_pct, pro)` with Performance display_group, included_limit=100, no overage. Migration `20260524210000_supabase_cpu_tracking.sql`. Auto-trip wiring deliberately deferred — sustained-vs-instantaneous threshold reasoning per the FIX-286 evaluator pattern is its own design problem. <!--id:FIX-355-->

The hardcoded 15 for Micro produced a misleading `18 / 15 = 120%` red bar even though Postgres's actual `max_connections = 60` cap was nowhere close. **Shape:** new SECURITY DEFINER RPC `get_supabase_max_connections() RETURNS INT` that returns `current_setting('max_connections')::INT` (STABLE, `SET search_path = public`, GRANT to authenticated + service_role — mirrors `get_supabase_auth_mau` from FIX-295). Snapshot job calls the RPC and writes through to `platform_limits.included_limit` for the `db_connections` row. Self-correcting on tier upgrades (Supabase adjusts `max_connections` automatically), no external API call, no lookup table to maintain. **Deletions:** `getSupabaseComputeTier()` + module cache, `clearSupabaseComputeTierCache()`, `SUPABASE_COMPUTE_POOL_MAX` constant, `poolMaxForTier()`, related types — plus their re-exports from `packages/db/src/index.ts` and the `compute_tier` / `pool_max` fields on the `/api/platform/supabase-prometheus` debug response. - [x] 🟠 S — **`rebuild_entity_connections()` statement timeout** — First successful GitHub Actions nightly (FIX-170) surfaced PG error 57014 ("canceling statement due to statement timeout"). Bump to `15min` in [supabase/migrations/20260430000000_rebuild_entity_connections_timeout_bump.sql](supabase/migrations/20260430000000_rebuild_entity_connections_timeout_bump.sql) — generous headroom for the same TRUNCATE + full-rebuild shape. If the function ever hits 15min in the future, that's the signal to refactor to incremental rebuilds rather than keep raising the cap. Caveat: PostgREST gateway timeout may also kick in around 60–120s for large RPCs; if we see HTTP 504 after the timeout bump, the call site needs to move off `admin.rpc()` to a direct Postgres connection. <!--id:FIX-171-->
- [x] 🟠 M — **Wire nightly to actually run via GitHub Actions** — Diagnosed during FIX-168/169: the Vercel cron route's docstring promised a "standalone scheduler at `packages/data/src/scheduler.ts`" would pick up triggers and call `runNightlySync()`, but that file never existed. So the Vercel cron has been firing into a void — the `cron_last_run` row in `pipeline_state` was only ever updated by someone running `pnpm data:nightly` from a laptop. (a) Add `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` running on `0 2 * * *` UTC, calling new script `pnpm --filter @civitics/data data:nightly:ci` (variant of `data:nightly` without `--env-file=.env.local` so secrets come from process env). Vercel cron is kept as a canary that confirms Vercel scheduler liveness, with docstring updated to reflect the actual architecture. (b) Fix a sibling of FIX-168: [packages/data/src/pipelines/index.ts:619](packages/data/src/pipelines/index.ts#L619) was inserting `data_sync_log` rows with `pipeline_name` instead of `pipeline`, swallowed by try/catch, so successful nightly completions weren't being recorded in `data_sync_log` either. **Required GitHub Secrets** (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions): `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, `CONGRESS_API_KEY`, `OPENSTATES_API_KEY`, `COURTLISTENER_API_KEY`, `REGULATIONS_API_KEY`. The Supabase URL is hardcoded in the workflow since it's public. <!--id:FIX-170-->
- [x] 🟠 S — **Move `vercel.json` into `apps/civitics/`** — The Vercel project's Root Directory is set to `apps/civitics`, so per [Vercel docs](https://vercel.com/docs/projects/project-configuration#vercel.json) `vercel.json` must live inside that directory to be discovered. With it at the repo root, the cron schedules in the file are never registered with the scheduler — which is why the 02:00 UTC nightly-sync hadn't fired (preceding FIX-168 fixed the route's correctness but not the registration). Move was a `git mv` so history follows. <!--id:FIX-169-->
- [x] 🟠 M — **Nightly cron correctness: data_sync_log column + Congress key name** — Two bugs that together explain why the dashboard "Last nightly" card has been showing stale data and Congress votes/officials have been silently skipped on every run. (1) [apps/civitics/app/api/cron/nightly-sync/route.ts](apps/civitics/app/api/cron/nightly-sync/route.ts) inserts `data_sync_log` with column `pipeline_name`, but the actual schema column (per [supabase/migrations/0022_data_sync_log_and_graph_snapshots.sql](supabase/migrations/0022_data_sync_log_and_graph_snapshots.sql)) is `pipeline`. The error is swallowed by the route's try/catch, so the trigger row never lands and the dashboard can't show that the cron fired. (2) Every Congress pipeline file uses env var `CONGRESS_API_KEY` (also what's in `.env.local`, `.env.example`, `turbo.json`), but the nightly orchestrator [packages/data/src/pipelines/index.ts](packages/data/src/pipelines/index.ts) checked `CONGRESS_GOV_API_KEY` — so the key was always "missing" and both `congress_officials` and `congress_votes` got status `skipped` regardless of whether the key was set. **Vercel env-var note:** if `CONGRESS_GOV_API_KEY` (and not `CONGRESS_API_KEY`) is what's currently set in Vercel, it needs to be renamed there for tonight's prod run to actually call Congress.gov. <!--id:FIX-168-->

- [x] 🟠 L — **Tag financial_entities with industry** — `chord_industry_flows()` joins to `entity_tags` with `tag_category='industry'`. Post-FIX-101 (FEC + USASpending) Pro has 2,639 financial_entities but zero industry tags, so every chord flow collapses to one "Untagged" bucket (~$60M+ Rep House etc). Need a rule-based or AI industry tagger pass — `financial_entities.industry` text column is already populated (CONNECTED_ORG_NM for FEC, empty for USASpending corps; NAICS code is in `financial_relationships.metadata->>'naics_code'` for contracts). Without this the chord visualization stays unusable. <!--id:FIX-109-->
- [x] 🟡 L — **Surface contract/grant flows in graph RPCs** — FIX-101 FEC + USASpending land `type='contract'` rows in `financial_relationships` (1,480 on Pro, more once grants land) and `contract_award` edges in `entity_connections`. All existing chord/treemap/donor-breakdown RPCs filter strictly to `relationship_type = 'donation'`, so government spending is invisible in any viz. Add `chord_contract_flows()` (agency → recipient sector / NAICS) and `treemap_recipients_by_contracts()` + wire them into a dashboard "Spending" panel. <!--id:FIX-110-->
- [x] 🟡 M — **Delete obsolete shadow-era pipelines after FIX-101 completes** — the following paths become dead code once the remaining FIX-101 rewrites land: `packages/data/src/pipelines/fec/index.ts` (legacy FEC API — CLAUDE.md already says "do not use"), `pac-classify/index.ts` (reads dropped `donor_name`), `financial-entities/index.ts` (reads dropped `donor_name`/`name`), `connections/shadow.ts` + `connections/delta.ts` (superseded by `rebuild_entity_connections()` SQL), `initiatives/shadow-backfill.ts` (one-time migration artifact), and the `shadowClient` helper in `packages/data/src/pipelines/utils.ts`. Remove in a dedicated cleanup commit — check `data:shadow-connections` / `data:shadow-initiatives` scripts in `package.json` too. <!--id:FIX-111-->
- [x] 🟡 S — **Fix `tags/rules.ts` broken column references** — rule runs during FIX-101 quick-wins verification logged two errors: `proposals.comment_period_end does not exist` and `financial_relationships.official_id does not exist`. Proposal tags and financial-entity tags paths both crash; only the officials path currently works (503 tags upserted clean). Update the queries to the post-cutover schema — comment_period_end lives on the proposal's metadata or a different column post-cutover; financial_relationships uses polymorphic `to_id`/`to_type`. <!--id:FIX-112-->
- [x] 🟢 S — **Explicitly paginate officials load in FEC bulk** — PostgREST default `max_rows=1000` silently truncates `loadOfficials()` in `packages/data/src/pipelines/fec-bulk/index.ts`. Pro is fine (~903 active federal officials, all fit), but local dev has 9,158 active officials (Legistar + OpenStates seed lots), so 8,158 get dropped during fuzzy-match builds — a latent correctness bug that would bite us any time the federal roster grows or we process state-level races. Use a pagination loop (range + offset) or a higher explicit limit. <!--id:FIX-113-->
- [x] ⬜ L — **Switch USASpending pipeline to award data archive (bulk download)** — current pipeline hits the paginated search API: hardcoded top-20 agencies, top 100 awards ≥ $1M, FY2024 only. USASpending publishes pre-built annual archives at `https://files.usaspending.gov/award_data_archive/` with predictable filenames (`FY2026_All_Contracts_Full_YYYYMMDD.zip`, `FY2026_All_Contracts_Delta_YYYYMMDD.zip`). Static files — no rate limits, no async polling, all agencies, all award sizes. Pattern is identical to the FEC `pas224.zip` streaming approach already in `packages/data/src/pipelines/fec-bulk/`. Implementation: (1) detect latest Full/Delta URL from the archive index page, (2) stream-unzip and parse CSV line-by-line filtering to agencies in our `agencies` table, (3) reuse `upsertSpendingRelationshipsBatch` writer. First run: Full file (~300MB–1GB compressed for partial FY). Subsequent runs: Delta file (much smaller). Supersedes current `data:usaspending` pipeline for contracts; FIX-114 grants fetch would also switch to `FY2026_All_Assistance_*.zip`. <!--id:FIX-118-->
- [x] ⬜ M — **Fix USASpending sub-agency attribution** — bulk pipeline only matched `awarding_agency_name`, so all Forest Service contracts landed on USDA and ICE/TSA/FEMA contracts were dropped entirely (not in agencies table). Fix: (1) seed ICE, TSA, FEMA as DHS sub-agencies via migration; (2) check `awarding_sub_agency_name` before `awarding_agency_name` in pipeline; (3) add stripped "U.S." alias keys to agency map so CSV names like "Department of Agriculture" match DB entries like "U.S. Department of Agriculture". Re-ran `--force` after fix: 841,264 matched (vs 837,417 before), 3,847 additional contracts correctly attributed. <!--id:FIX-119-->
- [x] 🟢 S — **Batch the reactive `findOrCreateBillProposal` path in congress bills** — the proactive sync is now batched (FIX-101 quick win) but the reactive path in `congress/votes.ts` still calls `findOrCreateBillProposal` per novel bill (3–4 RTs each — SELECT ref + INSERT proposal + INSERT bill_details + INSERT ref). Fires only for bills first seen during vote ingestion (typically a handful per run), so impact is low. If vote pipeline runtime grows, buffer novel bills during XML parse and flush in one batched pass at the end. <!--id:FIX-115-->
- [x] 🟡 S — **Tighten OpenStates people-endpoint rate limiting** — current `100ms` sleep between `/people` calls triggers 429s regularly (first call of each state, mid-chamber page turns). Each 429 costs a 30s retry stall; full 50-state run burns ~2–3 min of retry time even before the daily quota hits. Raise the inter-call sleep on the people endpoint to ~1000ms or add adaptive backoff that widens after each 429. Surfaced during the FIX-101 OpenStates Pro run (quota exhausted after 11 states partly due to cumulative retry waste). <!--id:FIX-116-->
- [x] 🟡 S — **Add index on enrichment_queue(entity_type, task_type) for snapshot reads** — the seed script's `fetchQueueSnapshot()` filters by (entity_type, task_type) without a covering index; at >50k queued rows each page scan becomes O(N) and hits Pro's ~8s statement timeout partway through. Seeded the Pro queue to 125,480 / 141,772 items; the ~17k gap is items whose classification fell inside a timed-out SELECT page. Adding `CREATE INDEX enrichment_queue_type_task ON enrichment_queue(entity_type, task_type)` makes the snapshot paginate cleanly; subsequent `data:enrich-seed` runs will then close the gap idempotently. <!--id:FIX-117-->
- [x] ⬜ M — **USASpending grants fetch** — FIX-101 USASpending rewrite queries `award_type_codes: ["A", "B", "C", "D"]` (procurement contracts only). Grants use codes 02/03/04/05/11 and land in a slightly different response schema. Post-FIX-101 Pro has 1,480 contracts and 0 grants. Add a second fetch pass against the grants codes if grant-level reporting becomes a product need — same batched writer, `relationship_type='grant'`. <!--id:FIX-114-->
- [x] 🟢 S — **USASpending bulk state per-environment** — `packages/data/.usaspending-bulk-state.json` tracks `lastArchiveDate` per category but not per env. After a local run records `20260406`, a prod run reads the same file, sees the date as already-processed, and exits without writing — current workaround is `--force` on every cross-env run. Key state under `envs.{supabase-url-host}.{category}` so `127.0.0.1:54321` and `xsazcoxinpgttgquwvuf.supabase.co` track independently. Migration: legacy per-category root state migrates into whichever env is active at first read; the other env starts fresh and needs one Full run. <!--id:FIX-166-->

- [x] 🟡 S — **Switch `packages/data/tsconfig.json` to bundler module resolution so subpath exports resolve** — [packages/data/tsconfig.json:6](packages/data/tsconfig.json#L6) uses legacy `moduleResolution: "Node"`, which doesn't read package.json `exports`. [packages/ai/package.json:7-13](packages/ai/package.json#L7-L13) declares subpath exports (`./cost-gate`, `./client`, `./cost-config`, `./cost-tracker`), so any `import … from "@civitics/ai/cost-gate"` fails type resolution under the data tsconfig — surfaced as 3× TS2307 errors at [ai-summaries/index.ts:30](packages/data/src/pipelines/ai-summaries/index.ts#L30), [tags/ai-classifier.ts:20](packages/data/src/pipelines/tags/ai-classifier.ts#L20), [tags/ai-tagger.ts:23](packages/data/src/pipelines/tags/ai-tagger.ts#L23). Validated: `module: "ES2022"` + `moduleResolution: "Bundler"` clears all three (TS5095 forbids bundler with module:CommonJS, so module needs the bump too). Runtime impact: `tsx` already understands both module modes, and `data` has no `tsc` build step — so flipping is safe. Worth confirming no other code paths assume CommonJS emit. <!--id:FIX-188-->
- [x] 🟡 M — **Stop importing `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and `@supabase/supabase-js` directly from `packages/data`** — Three files reach across workspace boundaries to packages they don't list as direct deps: [tags/ai-classifier.ts:18](packages/data/src/pipelines/tags/ai-classifier.ts#L18) and [tags/ai-tagger.ts:21](packages/data/src/pipelines/tags/ai-tagger.ts#L21) import `@anthropic-ai/sdk` (a dep of `@civitics/ai`); [scripts/copy-pac-tags-to-prod.ts:20](packages/data/src/scripts/copy-pac-tags-to-prod.ts#L20) imports `@supabase/supabase-js` (a dep of `@civitics/db`). Runtime works because pnpm's flat `.pnpm` store happens to expose them, but TS resolution fails (3× TS2307). Both directly violate the project conventions in `packages/db/CLAUDE.md` ("Import from `@civitics/db` — never directly from `@supabase/supabase-js`") and the same principle for `@civitics/ai`. Fix paths: (1) refactor the two AI tagger files to use `@civitics/ai`'s `createAiClient()` like `ai-summaries/index.ts` already does — keeps the Anthropic SDK behind the wrapper; (2) refactor `copy-pac-tags-to-prod.ts` to use `@civitics/db`'s admin client (or expose a small `createTwoEnvClients()` helper there since the script needs concurrent local + prod connections). <!--id:FIX-189-->
